name: University of Pittsburgh
header:
University of Pittsburgh
United States · Mathematics PhD
Ranking entry: 53. Current secondary ranking reports 53; official admissions evidence is independent of the ranking (s25).
Eligibility and preparation · Deadlines by stage · English and GRE · Academic records · Recommendation letters · Written
materials · Funding and fees · Conflicts and remaining checks · Faculty · Sources
Pay attention to
• Thomas Hales is emeritus and is not counted as an ordinary prospective adviser.
• Current profiles for Chou (machine learning), Pan (harmonic analysis) and Sparling (relativity/differential
equations) do not establish a close match to the requested algebraic/arithmetic/complex fields; they are not
added merely because of the broad word geometry.
• Do not substitute GradCAS’s platform-cycle closure for the department’s application deadline.

sections.title: Eligibility and preparation
sections.text:
Eligibility for your route [Standing rule]
Bachelor’s in mathematics or a related field; overall QPA >=3.0 and mathematics QPA >=3.25. Expected
preparation includes calculus, linear/abstract algebra, ODE, real and complex analysis. A UChicago math
bachelor’s is an eligible degree route; your grades and conferral date remain to be checked. F-1 status is not
an admission disqualification. [s1] [s2] [s3]
Before submission [Standing rule]
Apply through GradCAS; Pitt does not accept a paper application. Choose Mathematics/Dietrich and the
intended fall term. Request the fee waiver before paying. Prepare referees and resolve whether an unfinished
US degree qualifies for the English exemption. [s1] [s5] [s3]
Adviser contact [Standing rule]
No prior supervisor agreement is listed. The current group supports the four core matches below; ask about fall
2027 supervision before assuming availability. Department graduate office: jad432@pitt.edu. [s1] [s8] [s20]
Portal workflow [Standing rule]
GradCAS program-specific questions/documents control final upload rules. Submitted documents generally
cannot be edited/replaced, though a new optional slot may permit an additional document. The system’s
“2026-2027 cycle” label is not itself evidence of fall 2027 entry: select the actual term carefully. [s5] [s6]
Cycle verification [Conflict]
Admission deadline is a standing January 15 rule; advertised stipend amounts explicitly belong to 2026-27, not
2027-28. The English page is newer than department text still naming the 2025/26 DET season. [s1] [s3]

sections.title: Deadlines by stage
sections.text:
Academic application [Standing rule]
January 15 for the following fall (standing rule; the page does not explicitly label January 15, 2027). GradCAS
generally uses 11:59 p.m. Eastern Time; verify the selected program’s displayed deadline. Late consideration
is not promised. [s1] [s6]
Funding consideration [Standing rule]
Same January 15 standing deadline for admission and financial aid. No separately published first-year
fellowship deadline was located. [s1]

Reference receipt [Unresolved]
No separate departmental grace period is published. Treat January 15 as the complete-file target; the date you
type into a GradCAS request is your reminder date, not authority to extend Pitt’s cutoff. [s1] [s5]
Test-score receipt [Unresolved]
Separate score-receipt cutoff not published. If required, English scores must be official; GRE is optional. Allow
processing time before the January 15 target. [s1] [s7]
Supporting documents [Standing rule]
Application materials: January 15 standing target, without an independently published grace period. Final
certified transcripts, translations if needed, and bachelor’s conferral evidence are due at matriculation before
registration. [s1] [s3]
Accepting an offer [Unresolved]
The fall 2027 admission/funding response date was not established from these public sources. Read the offer
and current April 15-resolution participation; do not infer an admission deadline from an older signatory list.
[s1]

sections.title: English and GRE
sections.text:
English requirement [Conflict]
Dietrich accepts IELTS 7.0 (each >=6.5), DET 120, or TOEFL. For TOEFL from January 21, 2026: overall4.5,
speaking/reading/writing4.5 and listening5.0. Older departmental TOEFL threshold:90 with22 each; scores
normally valid two years. Use current Dietrich instructions for the new scale; confirm any mathematics-specific
higher standard. TOEFL code2927. [s3] [s1]
UChicago English exemption [Standing rule]
A completed degree from a regionally accredited US institution qualifies. Therefore a completed UChicago
bachelor’s meets the published degree route. The public wording does not expressly cover a bachelor’s still in
progress when applying; obtain confirmation. An admission waiver does not itself establish TA oral-language
certification. [s3] [s2]
GRE General [Standing rule]
Optional, encouraged if feasible; applications without scores receive full consideration. This is not a “not
considered” policy. [s1]
GRE Mathematics [Standing rule]
Optional, encouraged if feasible; not required. [s1]

Transcripts and degree records [Standing rule]
Upload undergraduate and applicable graduate transcripts for review. Official/certified final records and degree
evidence are required before registration; foreign-language records require certified English translations. No
external evaluation is specified for a UChicago-only academic record. [s1] [s3]

attachment is allowed, and its format/limit, must be checked in the program-specific GradCAS form. [s1] [s5]

sections.title: Recommendation letters
sections.text:
Number and type [Standing rule]
Three; referees should evaluate mathematical graduate-study potential. [s1]

Scholarship references [Unresolved]
No additional first-year scholarship reference is listed. Mellon is primarily a later second/third-year competition;
its separate future nomination/letter requirements were not established. [s1]
What sends the invitation [Standing rule]
In GradCAS, completing the request and clicking Save sends the referee invitation immediately. Merely
entering an unsaved name is not the documented trigger. [s5]
Before versus after submission [Standing rule]
Application submission is not needed to request letters; you can submit while letters remain outstanding. That
technical permission does not waive the program deadline. [s5] [s6]
Receipt confirmation [Standing rule]
An email confirms completion; the portal shows Complete and its date. Requested/Accepted statuses are not
receipt. GradCAS says references post immediately; transcript/score posting can take five business days. [s5]
[s7]
Updating and reusing letters [Standing rule]
Completed recommendations cannot be removed or replaced under the public GradCAS rule. New/in-progress
requests can be managed; wrong email requires delete/re-add. A previously entered referee can be selected,
but this sends a new request: automatic reuse of a completed letter across programs/cycles is not established.
[s5] [s6]

sections.title: Funding and fees
sections.text:
Amount and coverage [Prior cycle]
Published 2026-27 two-term stipends: TA USD24,050; teaching fellow USD25,000; Mellon USD25,000. Research
assistant range USD21,116-28,152 per two terms, undated “current” figure. Tuition remission and healthcare
accompany these awards. No fall 2027 rate, guaranteed summer amount or comprehensive mandatory-fee
coverage is established. [s1]
Years of support [Standing rule]
The handbook promises five years to full-time PhD students making satisfactory progress; a sixth may be

possible in special circumstances. Support usually covers fall/spring; summer depends on available work and is
not guaranteed. Master’s students have no general university funding guarantee. [s2]
International eligibility [Standing rule]
The admission/assistantship route includes international applicants; no citizenship exclusion is stated for the
departmental support described. Immigration/work and teaching-language requirements still apply. Exact
eligibility of any external award must be checked separately. [s1] [s3]
Conditions and duties [Standing rule]
Renewal requires satisfactory progress. TA/TF work includes undergraduate recitations/labs, office hours and
grading; research duties depend on the grant. Do not equate a fellowship with a work-free multiyear
departmental offer. [s1] [s2]
Extra funding application [Standing rule]
January 15 is explicitly the combined admission/financial-aid deadline. No extra first-year assistantship
application is listed publicly; confirm any program-form funding question. [s1] [s5]
Other funding routes [Standing rule]
Faculty-funded research assistantships and Mellon fellowships are additional routes; Mellon is aimed at
exceptional second/third-year students and carries no work duties beyond the program. It is not a guaranteed
first-year supplement. [s1]
Application fee [Standing rule]
USD75. [s1]
Fee waiver [Standing rule]
Dietrich offers case-by-case waivers through its linked survey; decisions normally within48 business hours,
Monday-Friday8:30a.m.-5p.m. Eastern. The published rule does not exclude international students, but
approval is not guaranteed. Request before paying. [s1] [s21]

sections.title: Conflicts and remaining checks
sections.text:
Conflicting sources [Conflict]
Department English text uses the old TOEFL scale and restricts its DET statement to 2025/26; Dietrich supplies
the new TOEFL scale and standing DET acceptance. Use the newer college policy, but confirm any
program-specific test rule. Some research-group descriptions label decades-old papers “recent”; faculty
evidence below instead uses 2025-26 records. [s1] [s3] [s20]
Checks still needed [Unresolved]
Confirm actual fall 2027 portal deadline and late-material rules; in-progress UChicago English exemption and
TA testing; all live attachment limits; scholarship-specific references; 2027 stipend, paid months, summer, fees
and response date; and new-student availability.

sections.title: Potential advisers and recent research
sections.text:
Algebraic / arithmetic geometry
Kiumars Kaveh
Newton-Okounkov bodies, toric/spherical geometry, valuations and tropical geometry; connections with
representation theory. [s8] [s9] [s10] [s11]
Professor on current Pitt roster; fall 2027 supervision unconfirmed.
Research evidence: 2025 · Toric Vector Bundles, Valuations and Tropical Geometry
Official University of Kentucky coauthor record; with Christopher Manon.

Roman Fedorov
Principal bundles and reductive groups, Grothendieck-Serre questions, Higgs bundles and motivic methods. [s8]
[s12] [s13] [s14]
Associate Professor on current roster; fall 2027 availability unconfirmed.
Research evidence: 2025 online · Unramified Grothendieck-Serre for isotropic groups
With Kestutis Cesnavicius; recent official publisher evidence supplements the older personal list.
Number theory
Carl Wang-Erickson
Galois deformation theory, modular forms, Eisenstein congruences and p-adic Langlands. [s8] [s17] [s18]
Associate Professor on current roster; fall 2027 availability unconfirmed.
Research evidence: 2026 preprint · Eisenstein congruences in tame families and the class group of a metabelian extension
Representation theory
Bogdan Ion
Double affine Hecke algebras, Macdonald theory, Lie-theoretic and affine flag/Grassmannian methods. [s8] [s15]
[s16]
Associate Professor on current roster; fall 2027 availability unconfirmed.
Research evidence: 2025 · The stable limit DAHA: the structure of the standard representation
With Dongyu Wu; official publisher record.
